entries.name: Preacher Curl
entries.reason: Source-bound draft repair: side view exposes the supported elbow arc; fixed upper arms on a connected sloped pad,12-unit circular forearm path,1000ms peak and3000ms full return.253 neutral grip and setup are bound to the frozen repo import; independent exact-source technique and native runtime acceptance remain pending.
entries.summary: Curl with supported upper arms, then return slowly to the start.

frames.caption: Support the upper arms on the pad and hold the bar with palms facing up.
Curl through the elbows while the upper arms stay on the pad.
Bring the load toward the shoulders without lifting the elbows.
Hold the top with the shoulders and upper arms quiet.
Lower on a three-count to the same natural long-arm start.

entries.name: Preacher Hammer Dumbbell Curl
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, from the description he accepted that day: the earlier drawing was a front view that could show neither the pad under the upper arms nor how far the arms straighten. Source-bound side-view draft: seated behind a sloping pad with the backs of both upper arms lying down its face; the upper arms do not leave the pad while the dumbbells are lowered slowly until the arms are almost straight, then curled back to shoulder height and held for a second. Each dumbbell stays square to its forearm, as a hammer is held.
entries.summary: Seated at a preacher bench with the upper arms on the pad and the palms facing each other, lower the dumbbells slowly until the arms are almost straight, curl them back to shoulder height and squeeze for a second.

frames.caption: Sit at a preacher bench and rest the backs of both upper arms on the pad, holding a dumbbell in each hand with the palms facing each other.
Lower the dumbbells slowly until the arms are almost straight and the biceps are stretched.
Curl both back up to shoulder height with the palms still facing each other.
Squeeze for a second. Upper arms stay on the pad.
